terms.gloss: a mountain chain, a mountain range
terms.grammar: noun phrase: montēs, montium m. pl., with perpetuus, unbroken
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase: mountains that run on without a break. Perpetuus is Pliny’s word for the unbroken ridges of the Apennines (below).

terms.gloss: a ridge; a chain of mountains
evidence: Lewis & Short: “a height or summit of a mountain, a ridge; also, a chain of mountains” (Verg. E. 5.76; Caes. BC 1.70)
M-O s.v. mountain range or chain
Traupman 202: Alpium juga, the Alpine chain
terms.comment: First a yoke; of mountains, the ridge, and so a range (see ridge). Morgan–Owens gives it for a mountain range, from the naturalists Desfontaines and Pallas.

terms.gloss: to stretch in an unbroken range
evidence: Plin. NH 3.48: Apennīnus perpetuīs jugīs ab Alpibus tendēns ad Siculum fretum (Lewis & Short s.v. perpetuus)
terms.comment: The verb phrase, for saying where a range runs: Pliny’s words, which Traupman borrows.

phrases.latin: nam Osoitsa ad rādīcēs Haemī jacet, quī perpetuīs jugīs per tōtam Bulgariam ad Pontum ūsque tendit
phrases.english: for Osoitsa lies at the foot of the Haemus, which stretches in an unbroken range across all Bulgaria to the Black Sea

phrases.latin: Appennīnus mōns perpetuīs jugīs ab Alpibus tendēns ad …
phrases.english: the Apennines extending in an unbroken chain from the Alps to …

sources: Lewis & Short: jugum · Lewis & Short: perpetuus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 201–203, 205.
